roadmap.goal: A slow test in the fast tier fails the build on both stacks and is named. The backend Integration tier has a mean ceiling that only goes down and a total ceiling that rises only by a reviewed entry with a reason. Each run shows count, sum and mean, and the three pyramid shares can be read with one command. No ci*.yml file changes and no product file changes.

dependencies.slice_a: Needs nothing from T6 #6512 or T5 #6469. It can run early, and it can go while T6 waits on CI: that is when the machine is free for its pnpm runs. Never beside a T6 test run or a dotnet build.
dependencies.slice_b: Needs T6 #6512 slice F on main, steps 06-02 to 06-05 pushed as T6's push 7. The connector scan reuses the base-chain walk of 06-02 and 06-03, both edit Scripts/test-timings/trx_to_csv.py, and until F labels the tiers there is no Integration row to count.
dependencies.slice_c: Needs T6 #6512 slice F for its first entries, one eligible plain backend run after it. The enforcing push also needs 5 distinct eligible runs after T5 #6469's last move or stop. T10 #6537 does not wait for it. T4 #6462 is already on main.

roadmap.notes: Rigor profile thorough: pass model explicitly on every dispatch, the profile's agent_model for crafters and reviewer_model for reviewers. Every step is executed by a crafter, so finalize finds phase entries for each; no step is orchestrator-only. A push is not a step: the orchestrator makes it after the step named in that step's implementation_notes. Slice A can go alone and early, ahead of T6, while T6 waits on CI. Slices B and C wait for T6's slice F, as roadmap.dependencies says. No non-test product code changes and no ci*.yml edit in any slice (D-6536-1, D-6536-21); a step needing one stops and reports. Mutation N/A in every slice, because Stryker mutates the product and no product file changes; the planted breach of each limit stands in (D-6462-20). Scenario ids A-1, B-1, C-1 and the kinds W, H, E, B, P name rows of the delta only. No nWave scenario tag and none of those ids goes into any test title, comment or file. Scenario rows, the report's words, the annotations and the decisions D-6536-31 to D-6536-47 are in feature-delta.md, sections Wave: DISTILL. Python tests run with python3 -m unittest discover -s Scripts/test-timings/tests. Frontend tests sit under Lighthouse.Frontend/src/tests/timeBudget and the gates are pnpm test and pnpm build, one at a time, never beside a dotnet build. Tests of the shipped budget file assert rules, never numbers (D-6536-27). The total ceiling is seconds only; option (b) is follow-up F-1 and is in no step. Before each push, T6's window check: git diff --name-only <last green> HEAD through each connector and shared classify_*, and a grep for ^.github/workflows/ci.*\.yml. Any true means wait for a green run or tell the maintainer. A conflict with trunk stops the step and reports; nothing is rebased. A red on trunk from a new ceiling follows DEVOPS 'A red on trunk'; LIGHTHOUSE_BUDGET_WARN_ONLY is the maintainer's to set, not an agent's. Slice C stays open and the Story stays Active while any limit is provisional; the chain moves on past it.

phases.name: Slice A: the frontend fast limit
phases.description: A second, lower limit in the Vitest reporter for every file that is not .test.tsx, then its figure from five shuffled runs. Needs nothing from T6. Mutation N/A: test tooling, no product file.

steps.name: A logic test has its own limit, still inert
steps.description: limitFor picks the base limit by the file's tier, ran-far-under-budget uses the test's own tier, the reporter prints both limits, and the config gets a new constant left at 2 s, so nothing changes yet.
criteria: Each of the delta's rows A-1 to A-8 is written in compareToAllowList.test.ts or timeBudgetReporter.test.ts and seen red for its own reason before the code changes
After the change they pass, and every existing case keeps its expected values; the shared options only gain the new field and the closing line of A-8 changes
Edge values sit off computed sums, as the delta says, because 0.6 x 3 and 0.6 + 0.31 are not exact in floating point
vitest.config.ts holds the new constant at 2, so a run's findings are as before
pnpm test and pnpm build pass with zero errors and zero warnings; git status is checked afterwards, as prebuild rewrites files
steps.scenario_name: A slow logic test fails the run and is named, and a component test of the same length does not
steps.implementation_notes: 8 scenarios. Run only while T6 waits on CI or has finished; never two test runs at once. Commit: feat(test-infra).

steps.name: The figure from five shuffled runs
steps.description: Re-read the 5 latest green shuffled frontend runs, set the limit by the rule, read the slowest file's local time, and prove the limit on real Vitest with a planted test.
criteria: The 5 latest eligible runs are read per job and attempt, D-6536-25, and their run ids, Vitest Duration and largest time in a file not ending .test.tsx are written in the delta, the slowest run seen among them
The limit is ceil(2.1 x L / 3) to 0.1 s; 0.6 s if L is still 0.726 s. If 5 eligible runs cannot be found the constant stays 2 s and the delta says so

One pnpm test:fast on a free machine: its time for layerBoundaries.enforcement.test.ts is written in the delta. If a test is over the limit there, it goes in slowTests.ts with a reason and a ceiling, and the delta names the risk that a listed test which moves between runs may retire itself

A-9: a planted .test.ts with two tests, the second past the limit, makes pnpm test:fast exit non-zero and name it; a planted .test.tsx of the same length passes under pnpm test on that file; both are removed and git status shows neither
pnpm test and pnpm build pass with zero errors and zero warnings
Before the push: git show --name-only of the slice's commits lists no .github/workflows path
steps.scenario_name: A real slow logic test fails pnpm test:fast, and the limit comes from five shuffled runs
steps.implementation_notes: 2 scenarios. Enforced from its first push; the frontend limit has no warn stage (D-6536-23). Push after this step: slice A alone, a Lighthouse.Frontend path, so backend is skipped and no live suite runs on a clean window. It may go while T6 waits on CI, but after T6's running CI run has ended, as ci.yml has no concurrency and each push waits for the one before. Commit: feat(test-infra).

steps.name: The enforcing push
steps.description: With 5 distinct eligible runs after T5's last move or stop, re-derive each limit, list what may be listed, and turn the limits on, on a clean window, read alone.
criteria: Entry: 5 distinct eligible ids after T5's last move or stop, each with a calibration row, the slowest seen among them; fewer means this step does not start, and the chain goes on past it
h is each figure's largest / smallest, at least 1.13. Spread over 1.25: no enforcing push for that figure, the maintainer is asked, and no run is removed to fix it
The fast limit is at least 2.1 x L; mean and total are largest x h, rounded up as D-6536-41 says
fast_allowlist holds only classes slow in all 5 runs, at most 10, each with a reason and a ceiling; a cost that moves between classes stays in L
The push goes on a clean window with no other push running; the first verdict is read alone and recorded
The commit touches test-time-budget.json, and slowTests.ts only if listed: git show --name-only shows no test file, and Test the budget check is green
No provisional warning is left. An enforced red follows D-6536-29: read the count, one re-run, then stop; the switch stays the maintainer's
The delta records the closing figures; the Story does not close while a limit is provisional
steps.scenario_name: Five eligible runs turn the limits on
steps.implementation_notes: 4 scenarios, C-4 to C-7. The only step that waits, and it blocks nothing but T9's closing. If T9 is still provisional at T10's end, T10 re-derives and T9 closes on that 5. Before T9 closes an agent may revert this commit to unblock trunk; afterwards that is a raise and needs the maintainer's word. Commit: test(test-infra).
